title: The ば / れば conditional
summary: ば is the hypothetical "if". Its hypothetical nature gives you advice (どうすればいい), regret (ばよかった) and obligation (なければいけない).

blocks.text: Where と says "this always leads to that", **ば** (also called れば) says **"suppose this"**. It is always "if", never "when", because it states a hypothesis, not a fact.

rows: 食べない → 食べなければ

blocks.text: The **え-stem** is the vowel row the ば form uses for godan verbs. Adjectives follow the same か-行 pattern: くない, かった, ければ.
Three expressions that come from hypotheticals
Japanese has no single word for "should" or "must". It uses a hypothetical instead, and that is why ば appears in so many set phrases. Think of する as "act" here.
**どうすればいい?** is literally "if I act how, would it be good?", which is "What should I do?"

blocks.jp: どうすればいいですか。

blocks.text: **〜ばよかった** is "if I had done it, it would have been good", which is regret: "I should have".

blocks.jp: 傘を持ってくればよかった。
blocks.en: I should have brought an umbrella.

blocks.text: **〜なければいけない** is "if I do not do it, it will not do": obligation. Casually it shrinks to **〜なきゃ**.

blocks.jp: もう行かなければいけない。

blocks.en: I have to go to bed early.

items: **どうすればいい**: what should I do?
**〜ばよかった**: I should have / I wish I had.
**〜なければいけない / 〜なきゃ**: must.
